title: FITS DATE-OBS records the END of the exposure, not the start - off by exactly EXPTIME
summary: Already fixed on this branch by an earlier fix batch, on BOTH paths the finding named. Manual capture: imaging_service.dart:399 now derives `observationStartedAt = captureTimestamp - exposureTime` and passes it as the FITS `timestamp` (lines 484/543/573) and as CapturedImageData.capturedAt; the code comment quotes the exact measurement from this finding ('a 30 s exposure starting 14:04:37 recorded 14:05:09'). Sequencer: FitsWriteHeaderRich::from_frame_context (api/imaging.rs:3480) now uses `ctx.exposure_started_at` instead of `chrono::Utc::now()`, falling back to now() only when no start was recorded.
test: Pre-existing Rust tests in native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs: `date_obs_is_the_exposure_start_not_the_readout_time` (asserts 2026-08-01T14:04:37, and explicitly NOT 14:05) and `date_obs_without_a_recorded_start_falls_back_to_now`. Not re-run here (cargo build is out of scope for this batch).
revert_check: n/a - no change made. Evidence is the current source: imaging_service.dart:399-401 and api/imaging.rs:3473-3483.
caveats: Verified by reading the current tree only. The end-to-end proof (write a FITS from a 30 s sim exposure and dump DATE-OBS) needs a native build, which this batch is not allowed to do.

title: Framing screen reports the wrong sensor size (1920x1080) for a camera that delivers 4144x2822
summary: Confirmed still present, and the verifier's correction is right: nothing in screens/framing is wrong. framing_provider/support.dart faithfully uses the geometry the camera ADVERTISES, and the simulated camera advertises SIM_W x SIM_H = 1920x1080 (api/devices/simulation.rs:73-74). The liar is the manual-capture generator in native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:824-825, which still hardcodes `let full_width = 4144 / bin_x; let full_height = 2822 / bin_y;` — so sim_frame.rs:36-42's claim that the three paths were unified ('the frame a caller receives matches the geometry the camera advertised') is still false. Simulator-only: on real ASCOM/INDI hardware the delivered frame matches CameraXSize, so no user with real gear gets a wrong FOV box.
test: None added — a truthful test would have to assert on the Rust generator I cannot edit.
needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:824-825 — replace the hardcoded 4144/2822 with `crate::sim_frame::SIM_W as u32 / bin_x` and `SIM_H as u32 / bin_y`, matching what SimulatedCamera advertises and what the sequencer/autofocus path already generates. Worth a Rust test asserting api_camera_get_last_image's width/height equal get_simulator_capabilities' sensor_width/height for every binning.
caveats: I deliberately did NOT add a 'sensor geometry disagrees' warning to the Framing sidebar. That would be disclosure-only: it would leave the simulator lying and add a scary banner that no real-hardware user should ever see.

title: Abort capture does not actually stop the exposure - the camera runs the full duration after "Exposure cancelled"
summary: Fixed the half that is real on BOTH sim and real hardware: the UI kept counting down an exposure the operator had already cancelled ('97% / 1.0s remaining' four seconds after the cancel). ExposureProgress goes on ticking after a cancel because the native waiter publishes progress until the driver reports not-exposing or the duration deadline passes, so the ring narrated a frame that was never going to arrive. The preview now drops the determinate ring, the percentage and the '…s remaining' line the moment an abort is issued and shows an indeterminate 'Stopping exposure...', and the toolbar's abort X is withdrawn (a second abort has nothing left to cancel). `_isStoppingCapture` is prop-drilled from the imaging screen into both children — one source of truth, no mirrored provider. The Dart side already issues a real abort (ImagingService.cancelExposure resolves the pending completer, which drives captureImage into _abortActiveExposure against the captured backend/device).
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/imaging/imaging_abort_countdown_test.dart — starts a real snapshot through the screen (stalled ImagingService), drives progress to 20%, taps the real abort key, then pushes two more progress ticks and asserts 'Stopping exposure...', no '…s remaining' anywhere, and no abort button.
revert_check: Deleted the production call-site argument `isAborting: widget.isStoppingCapture,` in live_preview_area.dart (the ExposureProgressOverlay construction): test fails with 'Found 0 widgets with text "Stopping exposure..."'. Restored -> green.
needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs api_camera_cancel_exposure (~line 1230): the `sim_` branch only sets `camera.status.state = Idle` and logs 'Exposure cancelled' while the exposure future sleeps on to completion — every real-device branch calls mark_camera_exposure_aborted + DeviceManager::camera_abort_exposure. The sim needs a real cancellation token the exposure loop polls, so a cancelled sim exposure ENDS. As it stands the simulator fails in the pass-making direction and cannot be used to validate abort at all.
caveats: The overlay stays up (indeterminate) until the device stops reporting an exposure. On the simulator that is still the full remaining duration, because of the native no-op above — the app now says 'Stopping exposure...' for that whole window, which is true, instead of counting down, which was not. Verification scope: `flutter test --exclude-tags golden test/screens/imaging test/screens/guiding` = 224 passed, `test/screens/framing` = 135 passed, `dart analyze lib test` = 0 errors/0 new warnings. The host-specific capture goldens (@Tags(['golden']), excluded from `melos run test`) fail on this machine independently of these changes - three of them are Guiding-screen captures and the Guiding screen imports nothing from screens/imaging.

title: The "1:1 zoom" button and the "100%" readout are fit-to-window - a 4144 px frame is shown at 987 screen px (23.8%)
summary: Root cause is that the preview had TWO meanings of zoom. ImagingViewerState.zoomLevel is documented as a multiplier relative to fit-to-window, and ImageDisplayWidget honours that (CustomPaint sized `constraints.constrain(imageSize)` then BoxFit.contain). But the toolbar printed `zoomLevel * 100` as if it were screen-px-per-image-px, AND — not previously reported — every overlay painter was handed the same raw multiplier together with computeImageOffset, whose `scaledSize = imageSize * zoomLevel` is native-scale arithmetic. Measured in a widget test: with a 2000x1200 frame in the preview the true scale is 0.437 while the overlays were told 1.0, i.e. star / annotation / catalog / celestial-grid / PSF / residual / uniformity / clip / moving-track markers and the scale bar were all spread over 2.3x (4.2x on the reported 4144 px sensor) their real footprint, landing on target only at the exact centre of the frame. New previewFitScale/previewDisplayScale helpers compute the scale the frame is really drawn at (including the no-upscale clamp for a frame smaller than the viewport); LivePreviewArea feeds that to computeImageOffset and all twelve overlay consumers and publishes it via previewDisplayScaleProvider, which the toolbar now reads for the zoom readout. Fit now reads its true percentage instead of '100%'.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/imaging/imaging_preview_zoom_scale_test.dart — pumps the real ImagingScreen with a 2000x1200 frame, measures the preview viewport, and asserts (a) the toolbar states the true percentage and never '100%' at fit, (b) the AnnotationOverlayWrapper the screen actually builds receives that same scale and an imageOffset matching the frame's real left edge.
revert_check: Reverted the wiring: `zoomLevel: displayScale` -> `zoomLevel: zoomLevel` at all twelve painter call sites plus computeImageOffset, and `_publishDisplayScale(displayScale)` -> `_publishDisplayScale(zoomLevel)`. Both tests fail ('Found 0 widgets with text "44%"'; overlay scale 'Actual: <1.0>' vs expected 0.4367). Restored -> green.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/imaging_viewer_state_provider.dart — the 1:1 button is still fit. `zoom1to1()` and `fitToWindow()` have byte-identical bodies (`zoomLevel: 1.0, panOffset: Offset.zero`) and the notifier exposes no way to set an arbitrary multiplier, so the screen cannot ask for zoomLevel = 1/fitScale. Needed: `void zoomToDisplayScale(double target, double fitScale) { state = state.copyWith(zoomLevel: (target / fitScale).clamp(minZoom, maxZoom), panOffset: Offset.zero); }`, plus lowering minZoom (0.25 today) so fit stays reachable — at 1/fitScale = 4.2 the existing maxZoom 8.0 is fine but a big sensor in a small pane can need a multiplier below 0.25 to return to fit. The imaging screen then calls it with ref.read(previewDisplayScaleProvider) / current zoomLevel as fitScale. Both consumers of that provider are files I own, so the core change is additive and low-risk. I left it out only because the file is outside my ownership list.
caveats: Until that method exists the '1:1 zoom' tooltip still describes a button that fits to window. The readout no longer lies about the result (it now shows e.g. 44%), but the control is still wrong. I did not add a note or rename the tooltip — that would be disclosure in place of a fix. Verification scope: `flutter test --exclude-tags golden test/screens/imaging test/screens/guiding` = 224 passed, `test/screens/framing` = 135 passed, `dart analyze lib test` = 0 errors/0 new warnings. The host-specific capture goldens (@Tags(['golden']), excluded from `melos run test`) fail on this machine independently of these changes - three of them are Guiding-screen captures and the Guiding screen imports nothing from screens/imaging.

title: The autofocus result overlay never auto-dismisses and follows the user onto every other screen, covering controls
summary: Confirmed real, and the finding's `where` is wrong: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/focus_panel.dart contains nothing about this overlay (grep for 'overlay' in that file returns nothing). The overlay is AutofocusProgressOverlay in packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/autofocus_progress_overlay.dart, mounted once in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:769 — deliberately shell-mounted (documented in the widget's own header as the single live V-curve surface), which is exactly why it follows the user onto Guiding / Plan Tonight / Framing. AutofocusOverlayNotifier.onAutofocusCompleted (skotiq_core .../autofocus_progress_provider.dart:225) sets isMinimized but leaves isVisible true with no timer, so the pill persists indefinitely. All three files are outside my ownership.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/autofocus_progress_provider.dart — onAutofocusCompleted should arm a ~10 s Timer that calls dismiss() (cancelled by any new run, by onAutofocusFailed, and in dispose); a FAILED run should stay up since it carries an error the operator must read. AND packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/autofocus_progress_overlay.dart + screens/shell/app_shell.dart:769 — while a run is IN PROGRESS the overlay is worth keeping shell-mounted, but a finished result should not float over unrelated routes; gate the completed-result pill on the imaging route (GoRouterState location) so it cannot cover the Guiding Tour card or the Framing rotation controls.
caveats: The verifier corrected one sub-claim: the collapsed pill's X does dismiss it cleanly; the reporter's click landed on the pill body, which re-expands. So the defect is persistence + global scope, not an undismissable widget.

title: False zeros: guiding peak error reads 0.00" with no guider, stack metrics read 0.00 px with no stack
summary: Imaging > Guiding tab: all five error tiles (RA/Dec/Total RMS + RA/Dec Peak) now read from ONE source (guideStatsProvider) and render an em dash until frameCount > 0 — the same gate the Guiding screen already uses. They previously came from two providers, and guiderState's copy of the RMS values is not cleared on GuidingStopped the way GuideStatsNotifier.reset() clears the source. Also stopped labelling guide-camera pixels as arcseconds (px unless a real pixelScale is known), which is the invariant guiding_no_measurement_readouts_test.dart already pins for the Guiding screen. Imaging > Stack tab: avgMatchedPairs / avgAlignmentResidual are per-ALIGNED-frame averages (imaging/src/stacking.rs divides by stacked_frame_count-1 because the reference frame is not matched against itself), so they dash out until stackedFrameCount > 1.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/imaging/imaging_panels_no_measurement_test.dart (5 tests) + the updated guiding_panel_peak_error_test.dart (2 tests, one new: arcsec only when pixelScale > 0).
revert_check: Reverted the guiding_panel readout block to `guideStats.peakRa.toStringAsFixed(2)` + `'$rms"'` and the two stacking_panel _StatRow values to the unguarded toStringAsFixed calls: 4 of the 5 new tests fail (the 5th is the control proving real values still render). Restored -> 5/5 green.
caveats: The same panel still labels the PHD2 settle tolerance (ditherSettings.settlePixels — guide-camera pixels) with a '"' suffix on the 'Settle Threshold' slider. Same class of unit lie, outside this finding, and it feeds golden screenshots, so I left it. Verification scope: `flutter test --exclude-tags golden test/screens/imaging test/screens/guiding` = 224 passed, `test/screens/framing` = 135 passed, `dart analyze lib test` = 0 errors/0 new warnings.
